ask.text: Today the library has 17 built-in button types (add, save, delete, cancel, download, print and so on). How many more should "exhaustive" mean? For example, a common set would add things like search, filter, copy, back, next, settings, help, info, warning, send, log in, log out, undo, approve and reject.
ask.why: It decides how many types and matching icons get designed, named, documented and tested, and how much the library grows in size.

options.label: A broad everyday set: about 25 to 30 more types covering the actions most apps need
options.consequence: Covers navigation, search and filter, clipboard, account, status and approval actions; each gets an icon, default look and documentation.

options.label: A small set: about 10 more types
options.consequence: Smallest growth and quickest to finish, but apps will still need custom types for common actions like search or copy.

options.label: Very wide: 50 or more more types
options.consequence: Almost nothing needs a custom type, but the library gets noticeably bigger and each type needs its own icon, docs and tests.

coverage.note: Developers who install the library and the people using their apps; no roles or permissions.
How many built-in semantic types are added decides the size of the work; names and icons follow from it.
A UI library has no records or ownership.
An unknown semantic type renders a plain button, as today.
Icons must keep working in the busy, success, fail and confirm states as today.
No submits or shared records are involved in defining types and icons.
Many buttons per page; icons must not be rebuilt on every render.
Builder chose the library's own SVG icons in one consistent style; the visible change to existing icons is noted in breaking-changes.

assumptions: The earlier toggle-mode decisions are already built and merged; this request does not change them.
